newsitem.title: USA: CME to monitor interest rate pits by video camera.
newsitem.headline: CME to monitor interest rate pits by video camera.

text.p: The Chicago Mercantile Exchange will use video cameras to monitor open outcry activity in its interest rate pits starting Thursday, the exchange said Wednesday.

The CME hopes its Video Trade Resolution System, which will be implemented as a pilot program for an unspecified period, will resolve disputes and outtrades without the CME's formal arbitration process.
"The Video Trade Resolution System will provide the trading floor with a reliable tool for resolving trade disputes quickly and efficiently," Rick Kilcollin, CME president, said in a statement.

The CME said 38 high-resolution cameras have been installed in fixed positions around its interest rate complex, and will record images on two videotape recorders so one tape can continue recording while the other is used to settle disputes.
Many disputes center around outtrades, or trades that have mismatched prices and quantities.

In open outcry, pit members trade by shouts and hand signals, with both the buyer and seller recording the transaction on paper. The transaction, including price and quantity, is then entered into a computer that matches buyers and sellers.

"When mistakes do occur, (the system) will enable the CME to correct them as fast as possible and focus on the business of enabling customers to manage risk," CME chairman Jack Sandner said in statement.
The tapes will be available for viewing immediately and for up to five days. The CME's arbitration committee will handle any disputes that cannot be resolved.
A CME spokesman would not say how many outtrades and disputes occur on an average day in any of the CME's markets, but he said the use of cameras might expand beyond the interest rate pits.
"If the system performs as we anticipate, then we will review expanding it to other complexes," he said. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuters.com))
